verdict.rationale: GitCafe's own webhook docs describe signed HTTPS requests sent to your server when repository or organization events occur, such as pushes, new issues or merged pull requests. That is a registrable outbound HTTP callback a programmatic consumer can receive. The evidence is a single first-party statement, so depth is thin. missing for 10: documented registration and configuration steps, event-type selection and filtering, signature-verification and retry/delivery-log details, independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can subscribe to events via webhooks

citations.quote: A webhook sends a signed HTTPS request to your server when something happens in a repository or organization, such as a push, a new issue or a merged pull request.
